## Getting the code running

Starting prompt (GPT-5.6 Luna Medium) : *I am doing a project where I am
investigating the central limit theorem and I need to see the smallest
sample mean value. The goal: Generate 10 graphs, two for each
distribution being tested. One graph will show kurtosis with sample mean
as the x axis and one will show skewness with sample mean as the x axis.
There need to be 10 individual graphs. I am working in R and the
distributions being tested are: generators \<- list( `Standard Normal` =
function(size) { rnorm(size, mean = 0, sd = 1) }, `Six-Sided Die` =
function(size) { sample.int(6L, size = size, replace = TRUE) },
Exponential = function(size) { rexp(size, rate = exp_rate) },
`R-Binomial` = function(size) { rbinom(size, size = binom_size, prob =
binom_prob) }, Cauchy = function(size) { rcauchy(size, location = 0,
scale = 1) } )*

This generated the start of my project. At first I had code that would
output all of the kurtosis and skewness plots on top of eachother and
because of the Cauchy distribution, all the other small values were
washed out. I needed something different.

I switched to Gemini 3.8 Flash

1.  *I need help with some R code. The code currently generates multiple
    plots inside one graph. I need it to instead generate multiple
    graphs (2X3) instead of 1 single graph. Here is my code please edit
    as necessary*

2.  *This is closer, I need the graph sizes to be parametric to each
    plot so they fully represent what is going on. Is a loop the best
    method for this?*

After getting it working with some small prompts I added the Q-Q chart

    normality for a distribution in reference to central limit theorem*

    (generated the Q-Q plot code)

adding more statistics for analysis

5.  

*can you implement measures for these and put them in a table for all of

## Starting the analysis

1.  Methodologies:

testing distribution at different stages of n)*

*Visual (graphs for skewness, qq, kurtosis etc)*

*Statistical Theoretical mean and standard deviation Simulated mean vs
theoretical mean simulated standard error vs SE*

*Write an example methodologies section for me going into each of these
listed above. Start a .qmd document and add the results there*

- This was the start of my CLT Framework document where I overview the

## Circling back to making the separate scripts

*Using this code as a template, generate me 5 individual R scripts (one
for each distribution). In these individual scripts I want the plots for
kurtosis and skewness and qq plots and others to only be for the
individual distribution associated with each script. The plots should
output onto one png all together. In addition to that I would like the
distribution to be plotted against a normal distribution for each sample
size. Each script should only contain plots and tables related to the
distribution it is for and none else. The X and Y on charts shoule be
appropriately scaled, not universally scaled.*

This prompt gave me 5 fairly complete documents that I could use to do
analysis on. I was not done yet however and had to make the document to
actually contain the analysis.

## Creating the separate analysis documents

*Using this code as a template, generate me 5 individual R scripts (one
for each distribution). In these individual scripts I want the plots for
kurtosis and skewness and qq plots and others to only be for the
individual distribution associated with each script. The plots should
output onto one png all together. In addition to that I would like the
distribution to be plotted against a normal distribution for each sample
size. Each script should only contain plots and tables related to the
distribution it is for and none else. The X and Y on charts shoule be
appropriately scaled, not universally scaled.*

This prompt generated the first analysis document which I formatted with
some help from the AI, asking it to add or drop small random things. One
bigger challenge was getting it to add working code to the documents and
I had a 30 minute frustrating session of errors that were resolved once
I realized I had created a typo.

With this boilerplate document, I ran the prompt:

*Taking this boiler plate example, create 4 more analysis documents for
each of the 4 other distributions*

This got me very close to the end product for analysis.

The rest of the project was finished by me filling in the blanks, making
sure the labels were correct and asking it to generate one final
analysis synthesis document.

The document it generated was a bit too specific and injected a lot of
analysis that was not my own so I asked it to shorten down the document
and made sure there was nothing that I couldn't explain or was not my
own opinion.
